opennyai_summary.facts:
These petitions have been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/
and Rs.5,00,000/ respectively for the injuries sustained by them in the Road Traffic Accident that took place on 12.08.2020.
4. Immediately after the accident the petitioner in MVC.No.3842/2022 was shifted to Narayana Hospital,
Ijoor, Ramanagar, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and discharged on 15.08.2020.
The respondent No.1 being owner and respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 contended that, both petitions filed by the petitioners are not maintainable either in law  6  MVC NO.3842 /2022  SCCH-10 or on facts and denied entire petition averments.
The claim petition is filed after lapse of 6 months from the date of accident, which is contradiction to the limitation specified.
The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA42A9400 in favour of respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent has denied the occurrence and mode of accident and the involvement of offending vehicle.
The driver of offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective DL and further the respondent No.1 has not possessed valid and effective permit and certificate to ply his vehicle on the road as on the date of accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal of the aforesaid documents it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Though the respondent No.2 has contended that the driver of the auto rickshaw had no valid Driving licence and the auto rickshaw had no valid permit, the investigation officer who at the time of filing charge sheet has not invoked any penal section for not possessing valid driving licence and violation of permit by the driver of the auto rickshaw.
19.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kamala Manga Lal Vayani and ors Vs M/s. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., reported n 2010 AIR SCW 6604 has held that,
 " The claimants are not expected to prove  that the vehicle had a valid permit, nor prove  that the owner of the vehicle did not commit  breach of any terms of the policy, it is for the  insurer who denies his liability under the policy  13  MVC NO.3842 /2022  SCCH-10 Jayakumari .K.J vs Jyothi Prakash D on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82932142/
10  to establish that inspite of comprehensive  issuance of policy issued by it, it is not liable  on account of requirements of the policy not  being fulfilled."
20. Further Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the judgment reported in 2010(1) AIR Kar R 202 in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bangalore Vs Smt. Mahadevamma & Ors, held that the violation of terms and conditions of permit is a ground for cancellation of permit, but same cannot be a ground for insurance company to absolve from its liability to pay compensation.
23. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicle accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.
This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.
Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the  15  MVC NO.3842 /2022  SCCH-10 materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA42A9400.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income.
In the present case, there is no disability caused to the petitioner and there is no loss of future income.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore, in the instant case, though the petitioner has contended that, she has permanent  21  MVC NO.3842 /2022  SCCH-10 disability, the said disability will not result in loss of future earning capacity.
31. The petitioner has contended that due to the injuries, she cannot do any work by using her right hand.
